correctness.rationale: The original antipodal-pair claim at r=1/2, a=−1/4, c=1 is false if it refers to positivity of the whole pair: 4/5 tests only the antisymmetric vector. For u=b cos(2x), the eigenvalues of the antipodal Gram matrix are (p+q)(a+(c+u)/μ) and (p−q)(a+μ(c+u)), with p=P_r(0), q=P_r(π). Requiring both yields |b|≤min(c+μa,c+a/μ)=11/16 in the example. In particular b=4/5 and x=π/2 give eigenvalue −3/10. The complete corrected result derives both eigenvalues; 67/100 still satisfies every antipodal test and violates the full PSD bound. Independent exact evaluation recovers the indicated eight-site energy −1217/1275 and minimum diagonal 6/25. The main theorem survives unchanged: direct Fourier expansion gives even/odd Jacobi sectors, and approximating trigonometric-polynomial densities by atomic measures proves necessity on all weighted finitely supported Fourier vectors. The repaired odd-sector argument uses a positive eigenvector supported with geometric tails of ratio r and the sum-of-squares ground-state identity; sign alternation gives the opposite extremum. The even-sector bulk bottom is h−|b|; an attractive defect −cδ yields h−sqrt(b²+c²δ²) by matching the unique decaying solution on the two tails and the origin, and a nonattractive defect cannot lower the bottom. The diagonal b=0 case gives the same formula. At odd equality an antipodal antisymmetric vector is null (or the b=h=0 kernel is constant). At strict odd margin a possible even zero mode has ratio |t|<r per step of two indices, so its unweighted even Fourier sequence tends to zero despite F_0≠0. Cesàro orthogonality rules this out for finite atomic measures, including the b=0 constant-Fourier-mode nullspace. Fourier uniqueness excludes the zero sequence for a nonzero distinct-site vector. This checks the repaired theorem, example, and endpoints without a finite-to-infinite extrapolation.
residual_risks: The scope is the given first-harmonic mixed kernel at a fixed 0<r<1; distinct-site strictness is not a uniform lower bound across node sets.
